[panda1010101] Agreed, mods should enforce a limit. Is this considered sockpuppeting?
[darkly] Not sure if it is sockpuppeting, but it does look like it is exceeding the posting limit:
"Representatives are able to post a maximum 1 deal per 24 hours and maximum of maximum 2 deals per 7 days provided previous deals have been well-received. Please see the posting limits page for more details."
[Clear] The system won't let a rep post if their posting limit has been reached.
[NEWLAND] Hi, friend. Our posting behavior follows the website's rules. We also did not use multiple accounts or fake reviews.
[Clear] You can't be considered a sockpuppet if you've declared association.
[scrimshaw] The limit is the same for every merchant. Explained here. 2 every 7 days (rolling window) but actual limits are decided by the community. .
TLDR: More votes = more posts allowed. Less votes, or no votes = Less posts.
Note that users who spam + votes on a lot of deals will cause the system to 'ignore' their votes when calculating performance.
Posting limits are calculated automatically by the system. If they have hit the limit, they get an error message when attempting to post.
Is this considered sockpuppeting?
No. Sockpuppeting is when….
The deal poster pretends to be someone they are not and writes the deal as if they are not associated with it
There are associated individuals using Ozbargain accounts to upvote the deal to push it to the front page OR they write false positive comments or pretend to be a customer in the comments, or otherwise commenting without declaring association.
When the deal poster themselves creates multiple accounts and uses them to boost their posts (upvoting the deal etc)
[mickeyjuiceman] Did you consider, oh, I don't know, looking at the definition of sockpuppetting, or do you just like the word as a general term of disapproval?
[NEWLAND] Thank you for your comment.
The reason we're updating these product discounts is that many people asked us to notify them when these products were back in stock, and others commented on previous posts saying they wanted discounts for them. We're not mechanically posting spam without any reason—we're sharing updates because there is genuine demand.
If you don't need the product right now, any promotional post may seem like spam to you. But many people do have this need, otherwise we wouldn't keep posting these updates.
Compared with other mechanical keyboard brands, we've genuinely lowered our prices to offer real discounts.
To provide better service and better deals, we've also set up a warehouse in Australia, which will be operational next month.
If our post has disturbed you, I sincerely apologize.
[TheBardsTale] Or you could just reply to their comments…
[mickeyjuiceman] It must be tough having to click on every post, yeah
[TheBardsTale] It's annoying getting a notification that there is a mechanical keyboard bargain and find out it's this crap
[Supercool] The perpetual sale. I've got notification for keyboards, and keep getting spammed with this ozmarketing.
[carrawa] @Supercool: Is there a way to remove specific del posters from notifications?
[Dday1] Do you have any wireless keyboards with a numpad on sale?
